title: The Weil structure of field-coefficient compact support commutes with shifts
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0=\mathbf F_q,k=\overline{k_0}$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated finite-type morphism of quasi-separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let $f:X\to Y$ be its base change to $k$, and let $g_X,g_Y$ be the geometric Frobenius automorphisms of $X,Y$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Let $\Lambda\in\{E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$, with the rationalized category $D^b_c(-,E)$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] or the common-stage category $D^b_c(-,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], and let $Lg_X^*,Lg_Y^*$ be the derived pullbacks [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; these are computed by termwise inverse image and so commute with the shift functors, $Lg^*(M[r])=(Lg^*M)[r]$. For a $\Lambda$-Weil complex $(M,\theta_M)$ on $Y_0$ or $X_0$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] and $r\in\mathbf Z$, give $M[r]$ the Weil structure $\theta_M[r]$. Let $Rf_!:D^b_c(X,\Lambda)\to D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$ be the compact-support functor [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], with its shift comparison $\sigma_{K,r}:Rf_!(K[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}(Rf_!K)[r]$ as an exact functor [lem-zl-field-shriek-lower-bound], and for a $\Lambda$-Weil complex $(K,\theta_K)$ on $X_0$ let $\theta_{Rf_!K}=Rf_!(\theta_K)\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{!,K}$ be the canonical Weil structure on $Rf_!K$ [lem-fix-weil-operations]. Then for every $\Lambda$-Weil complex $(K,\theta_K)$ on $X_0$ and every $r\in\mathbf Z$,
$$\sigma_{K,r}\circ\theta_{Rf_!(K[r])}=\theta_{Rf_!K}[r]\circ Lg_Y^*(\sigma_{K,r}):Lg_Y^*Rf_!(K[r])\longrightarrow(Rf_!K)[r],$$
that is, $\sigma_{K,r}$ is an isomorphism of Weil complexes $(Rf_!(K[r]),\theta_{Rf_!(K[r])})\to((Rf_!K)[r],\theta_{Rf_!K}[r])$. No separatedness of $X_0$ or $Y_0$ over $k_0$ is assumed.
